title: Facilities & Field Sites
intro: Two analytical suites, a calibration bench and three field stations — the places our measurements are made.
add_paragraph:
Most of what the lab knows begins somewhere cold, wet or dusty, and ends on a bench in TerraNova. The rooms and the stations are not scenery: the way a sample is handled in the first hour decides what it can still tell us a year later.

We keep the bench close to the field teams. Instruments are calibrated here, deployed from here, and opened here again when they come back — often on the same day.

add_image.image_caption: The analytical suite, before the morning run.

add_list.heading: Rooms, roofs and stations
add_items_to_list: **The trace lab** — clean benches, reference instruments and the mass spectrometers that carry most of our analytical work.
**The sensor bench** — calibration ovens, a humidity chamber and the lab's own reference loggers, kept within a degree of each other.
**Storglombreen station** — the alpine site, open May to September, with power and shelter for three field teams.
**Station Nord-03** — the coastal station, shared with the institute's marine group, a short walk from the mangrove plots.
**The green-roof array** — paired planted and bare roofs across the city, instrumented for the three-summer survey.

add_special_note.heading: Visiting
add_special_note.text: The lab hosts visiting researchers and student groups. Write to {the lab|@contact} before planning a trip — bench space and station beds are limited in the field season.
